howToExport: Log in to PayPal on the web and go to Activity.
Click the Download icon and choose Custom; pick the date range (one request covers up to 12 months).
Select CSV as the format and keep the default fields (Date, Name, Type, Status, Currency, Gross, Fee, Net, Balance…).
Download the report once PayPal says it's ready (large ones take a while), then add it above.
knownQuirks: PayPal's Net column is what reaches your PayPal balance. With the gross/fee split on, a Gross line and a Fee line replace each Net line and still add up to it to the cent.
Pending, denied and voided rows are dropped using the Status column, so authorisations that never settled don't land in Xero.
A refund that returns part of the fee produces a positive fee line: the split works the fee out from Gross and Net, so PayPal's sign conventions don't matter.
Currency conversions show up as paired rows. If your file mixes currencies, pick one per import, as a Xero bank account holds a single currency.
